steps.stem: Professor Almagor's lecture was based almost entirely on ____ , and therefore it had the character of ____ . All the more surprising, then, that in the middle of this ____ lecture he stopped several times in order ____ .
choices: detailed statistical tables / a technical report / dry / to tell the audience about his childhood in Tiberias
quotations from legal documents / an official document / formal / to read aloud the exact wording of several laws
personal stories / a dry academic paper / lively / to tell another story from his own life
short and simple sentences / a talk with children / light / to ask the audience easy questions
explanation: Only stories about his childhood clash with a dry lecture built on tables, so only (1) justifies "surprising". In (2) and (4) the last part fits the character of the lecture, so nothing is surprising; in (3) personal stories cannot give a lecture the character of a dry academic paper.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Opponents of the new examination method that was introduced in the school claim that since it was introduced, ____ . The principal, Harel, ____ this, ____ , since ____ .
choices: the teachers spend less time checking each examination / confirms / and adds that this was not his intention / the method was meant to save the teachers' time

the teachers spend much more time checking each examination / does not deny / but claims that this is exactly the purpose of the method / only in this way can each student receive a detailed comment on his work
the teachers spend much more time checking each examination / admits / and explains that this is exactly what he expected / the method was meant from the start to save the teachers' time
the students receive fewer comments on their work / rejects / and claims that this is exactly the purpose of the method / the students are expected to find their mistakes by themselves
explanation: Harel concedes the critics' point (more time) and presents it as the purpose of the method, which the detailed comments explain. In (1) the method saves time as it was meant to, so "this was not his intention" makes no sense; in (3) a method meant to save time cannot be expected to take more time; in (4) he rejects a claim and at the same time calls it the purpose of the method.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.title: Sentence completion - connectors and method
steps.intro: The link between the parts of the sentence decides the answer. Know the connectors by what they do.

tables.title: Connectors by function
head: Link
English connectors
rows: Contrast
but · however · although · even though · despite · nevertheless · yet · whereas · unlike
Concession
admittedly … but · does not deny … but · even if · even so
Cause / result
because · since · owing to · therefore · thus · for this reason · so
Addition
and · moreover · and even · likewise · not only … but also
Detail / example
for example · such as · that is · a colon ( : ) · a dash ( - )
Condition
if · unless · only if · provided that
Hypothetical
had … / were … (= if) · had it not been for · were it not for · but for (= if not)

tables.title: The method
head: Step
What to do
rows: Shrink the sentence to its skeleton: cross out noise, rewrite hard parts briefly
Many negatives? Write signs above the blanks: Y / N (refused, without, lacks… = N), ↑ / ↓ - compare signs
Read with an option in place - never with holes
Plug in by similar beginnings; predict how the sentence should go on
Parts contradict each other → eliminate (the sentence’s logic, not world knowledge)
Down to two? Go to the last blank - does it deliver what the key word promises?
It fits → a quick look at the other options, then mark it and move on

tips: Hypothetical: what really happened is the reverse of what is written.
Had it not been for X, Y would… → because of X, not Y.
A hunch may choose which option to try first - never mark without checking.

steps.stem: ____ found that the inspector's report, according to which the old building is safe, was ____ , the residents would not have been ____ their apartments.
choices: Had the engineer / reliable / allowed to stay in
Had the engineer not / inaccurate / allowed to stay in
Had the engineer / inaccurate / ordered to leave
Had the engineer not / inaccurate / ordered to leave
explanation: What really happened is the reverse of what is written: the engineer found the "safe" report inaccurate, so the residents were ordered to leave. (2) makes the residents stay although the report was rejected; (1) and (3) use a positive condition that gives the opposite result.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: ____ that Tamar generally refuses to lend her tools, ____ when she ____ her new drill.
choices: Had I known / I would have been hurt / refused to lend me
Had I not known / I would have been hurt / offered to lend me
Had I not known / I would not have been surprised / offered to lend me
Had I known / I would not have been surprised / agreed to lend me
explanation: Because I knew that Tamar does not lend her tools, I was surprised when she offered me her drill. In (1) knowing would prevent the hurt; in (2) no one is hurt by an offer; in (4) knowing is exactly what would cause the surprise.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Many residents objected when the municipality spent most of its budget on ____ . After the heavy rains of last winter, however, ____ , because ____ .
choices: raising the walls of the reservoir / the objections only grew / the higher walls kept the water out of the lower streets
repairing the roads / most of the objectors admitted that the money had been well spent / the reservoir overflowed and flooded the lower streets
raising the walls of the reservoir / the residents stopped objecting / the water rose even above the new walls
raising the walls of the reservoir / most objectors admitted that it had been worth it / otherwise the lower streets would have flooded
explanation: The higher walls saved the lower streets, so the objectors changed their minds, as in (4). In (1) the objections grow although the walls did their job; in (2) a flood from the reservoir does not show that money spent on roads was well spent; in (3) walls that failed give no reason to stop objecting.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Although the results of the study ____ that the stomach illnesses in the village were caused by the water of the old well, the village council ____ , and the well ____ .
choices: strongly supported the suspicion / refused to accept them / remained in use for another two years
did not support the suspicion / accepted them / was closed the following week
confirmed the suspicion / accepted them at once / was closed that same month
strongly supported the suspicion / decided to close the well / was sealed within a few days
explanation: Results that support the suspicion, and yet the council rejects them and keeps the well open: a real contrast, as in (1). In (3) and (4) the council acts as the results suggest, so "Although" does not fit; in (2) the council accepts results that do not support the suspicion, which is no contrast either, and then closes the well anyway.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The five members of the jury ____ about which film should win the prize; ____ , when they were asked what they had looked for in the films, they all ____ .
choices: argued for hours / nevertheless / gave almost the same answer
agreed within minutes / nevertheless / gave almost the same answer
argued for hours / therefore / named the same three qualities
could not agree / however / gave completely different answers
explanation: A long argument about the winner contrasts with an almost identical answer, as in (1). In (2) quick agreement and the same answer are no contrast; in (3) the same answer does not follow from the argument; in (4) different answers are no contrast to the disagreement.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: If ____ did not convince the members of the committee that the plan was dangerous, then all the more so ____ will not ____ .
choices: the rumors that spread in the town / the detailed report of the engineers / convince them
a single complaint from one of the residents / hundreds of complaints / persuade them
the detailed report of the engineers / the rumors that spread in the town / fail to convince them
the detailed report of the engineers / a few rumors / convince them
explanation: "All the more so" moves from strong evidence that failed to weaker evidence, which will surely fail as well, as in (4). (1) and (2) move from weak evidence to strong; in (3) the conclusion says that the rumors will convince them.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem:
Hadas: "The journalist who pretended to be a clerk in order to get the minutes of the meetings ____ , because thanks to him the public learned of the failures."
Amnon: "____ , since the minutes ____ ."
choices: acted rightly / Your argument does not hold / could not have been obtained in any other way
acted rightly / Your argument does not hold / have been open to the public in the library for years
should be condemned / I agree with you / were published anyway a week later
acted rightly / That is true / had already been published a year earlier
explanation: If the minutes were open to all, the deception was not needed to inform the public, so Hadas's argument fails, as in (2). In (1) Amnon's reason supports Hadas; in (3) Hadas's reason does not support condemning him; in (4) Amnon agrees but gives a reason against her.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Although the new spelling rules ____ , most of the older writers ____ , ____ .
choices: made texts easier to read / adopted them at once / because they found them simpler
made texts easier to read / went on writing in the old way / mostly out of habit
were confusing and full of exceptions / went on writing in the old way / because they did not understand them
were approved by the language academy / adopted them / as the academy had asked
explanation: Simpler rules and yet no change, explained by habit, is a real contrast, as in (2). In (1), (3) and (4) the writers do what the rules' qualities lead us to expect, so "Although" does not fit.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: It is ____ that each of the two research teams tried to publish its results before the other, ____ .
choices: strange / since both were working on the same problem
not surprising / since they had agreed to publish their results together
not surprising / even though they were competing for the same discovery
not surprising / since they were competing for the same discovery
explanation: Competition for the same discovery explains the race to publish, as in (4). In (1) the shared problem explains the race, so it is not strange; in (2) an agreement to publish together makes the race surprising; in (3) "even though" presents the explanation as an obstacle.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The researchers expected that the new fertilizer ____ the yield of the wheat, since ____ . The yield, however, ____ , and the researchers ____ .
choices: would increase / it contains a great deal of nitrogen / rose as expected / were pleased
would not affect / it contains a great deal of nitrogen, which wheat needs / fell / cannot explain why
would increase / wheat grows poorly in soil rich in nitrogen / fell / found this puzzling
would increase / it contains the nitrogen that wheat needs / did not change / still have no explanation
explanation: The reason supports the expectation and the result contradicts it, as "however" and the missing explanation require in (4). In (1) the result confirms the expectation; in (2) and (3) the reason given does not support the expectation.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Some claim that translation ____ the language into which books are translated, since ____ ; ____ , others claim that translation ____ .
choices: impoverishes / translators tend to use only the most common words / similarly / has brought many new words into the language
enriches / translators tend to use only the most common words / in contrast / has done the language much harm
impoverishes / translators tend to use only the most common words / in contrast / has brought many new words into the language
enriches / translators must find words for new ideas / therefore / has made the language poorer
explanation: The first claim and its reason agree, and the second claim opposes it, as "in contrast" requires in (3). In (1) "similarly" joins opposite claims; in (2) the reason contradicts the first claim; in (4) "therefore" introduces a claim that contradicts the one before it.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: In the opinion of the teachers at a certain music school, students should choose for themselves which pieces to practice and for how long. However, at the beginning of every year the teachers prepare for each student a list of pieces suited to his level, and the student chooses only from this list. ____
choices: Therefore, the students of this school practice only the pieces that their teachers choose for them, and only for as long as the teachers allow.
Thus, in the teachers' view, the freedom to choose does not require that the choice be unlimited.
Therefore, the lists that the teachers prepare have no influence on the pieces that the students practice.
Thus, the students may practice any piece they wish, whether or not it appears on the list.
explanation: The teachers let the students choose, but only from a list, so in their view free choice can be limited, as in (2). (1) contradicts the students' own choice; (3) and (4) contradict the fact that the students choose only from the list.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the dots separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Tamar believes that a team in which ____ reaches ____ . She therefore hopes that she is ____ in thinking that the members of her new team ____ .
choices: everyone agrees / poor decisions / wrong / often disagree
there are many arguments / poor decisions / right / often disagree
there are many arguments / better decisions / wrong / agree about almost everything
everyone agrees / better decisions / wrong / agree about almost everything
explanation: Tamar values arguments, so she hopes that her impression that her team agrees about everything is wrong, as in (3). In each of the other options her hope leads to the kind of team that she herself considers worse.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The ____ report on the state of the forests in the north ____ . "____ ," say ____ .
choices: alarming / did not worry anyone in the ministry / Only if money is found at once / officials in the ministry, "will the forests be saved"
encouraging / pleased the foresters / This is good news / the foresters, "we have lost most of the young trees"
alarming / worried the authorities / There is hope / the authors of the report, "that nothing can be done"
encouraging / did not calm the foresters / More money is still needed / the foresters, "or the forests will not recover"
explanation: Good news that is not enough, so the foresters ask for more money, as in (4). In (1) officials who are not worried demand urgent money; in (2) and (3) the quotation contradicts what comes before it.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The songs of the poet Oren ____ in his lifetime, and only thirty years after his death, when ____ , did they become known. ____ his name is familiar today to most readers of poetry.
choices: were read by many / a critic found them in an old notebook / It is thanks to that critic that
were hardly read / his son published them against his wishes / Despite this,
were hardly read / a critic found them in an old notebook / It is thanks to that critic that
were hardly read / they were completely forgotten / Thanks to this,
explanation: Songs that were hardly read became known through the critic, and he is the reason for the poet's fame, as in (3). In (1) songs read by many could not become known only after his death; in (2) the publication explains the fame, so "Despite this" does not fit; in (4) songs cannot become known at the moment they are forgotten.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: In the nineteenth century the towns of the region grew ____ than the villages, ____ in years of drought, when ____ .
choices: faster / especially / many farmers left their land and moved to the towns
faster / except / many farmers left their land and moved to the towns
more slowly / especially / many farmers left their land and moved to the towns
faster / especially / hardly anyone left the villages
explanation: Farmers moving to the towns in drought years explain why the towns' lead was largest then, as in (1). In (2) the towns stop leading exactly when farmers move into them; in (3) the towns grow more slowly especially when they gain people; in (4) nothing explains why the drought years were special.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The lawyer told his client that the arguments in the appeal that had been filed ____ him ____ , but that since the court ____ appeals of this kind, it is ____ that this appeal too will be rejected.
choices: against / are weak / almost always rejects / quite possible
against / are not groundless and are supported by several earlier rulings / usually accepts / likely
against / seem convincing / has accepted very few / quite possible
by / have no legal basis / has often accepted / certain
explanation: "But" requires a contrast between strong-looking arguments and a real chance of rejection, as in (3). In (1) weak arguments and frequent rejection are not a contrast; in (2) and (4) the court's record does not support the expected rejection.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Unlike most of the members of the council, Na'ama ____ the plan to demolish the old station building. In her opinion, they supported the plan ____ they knew that ____ .
choices: supported / because / the building was in danger of collapsing
opposed / precisely because / it was the oldest building in the town
opposed / although / the building was in danger of collapsing
opposed / even though / it was the oldest building in the town
explanation: Na'ama opposes the demolition, and the others support it despite knowing the building's value, as in (4). In (1) she does not differ from them; in (2) the building's value is given as their reason for demolishing it; in (3) a danger of collapse is a reason for demolition, so "although" does not fit.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: It is ____ that Yifat, who ____ her father's opinion that ____ , sends her own children to ____ .
choices: not surprising / has always shared / small schools are better for children / the largest school in the city
surprising / has always shared / small schools are better for children / the largest school in the city
surprising / has always rejected / small schools are better for children / the largest school in the city
not surprising / has always shared / large schools offer children more / a small village school
explanation: Someone who shares the view that small schools are better yet chooses the largest school acts against her own opinion, which is surprising, as in (2). In (1) and (4) her choice contradicts her opinion, so it is not "not surprising"; in (3) her choice follows from rejecting that opinion.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The findings of the survey ____ the common belief that ____ , since they showed that ____ .
choices: refute / most birds of this species leave the valley in winter / most of them stay there all year
support / most birds of this species leave the valley in winter / many of them stay there all year
refute / most birds of this species stay in the valley all year / many of them stay there in winter as well
confirm / the birds of this species never leave the valley / most of them spend the winter in the south
explanation: If most of the birds stay all year, it cannot be that most of them leave in winter, so the belief is refuted, as in (1). In (2) and (4) the findings contradict the belief that they are said to support; in (3) the findings agree with the belief that they are said to refute.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: After Gilad failed his driving test, his instructor told him: "____ the heavy rain, you ____ , because ____ ."
choices: Had it not been for / would have passed / in all your lessons, even on dry days, you made the same mistakes
Even without / would not have passed / in all your lessons, even on dry days, you made the same mistakes
Had it not been for / would have passed / you drove perfectly in all your lessons, including those in the rain
Even without / would have passed / you had never driven in the rain before
explanation: Mistakes made on dry days show that the rain was not the cause, as in (2). In (1) and (3) the reason contradicts the claim that the rain caused the failure; in (4) "even without the rain you would have passed" makes no sense for a test he failed, and the reason points to the rain.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The violin solo was performed at a level that ____ the level expected of soloists in the country's leading orchestras. ____ amazed to learn that the performer was ____ a twelve-year-old student, ____ a seasoned professional.
choices: falls far short of / I was therefore / none other than / from whom one cannot expect playing like that of
is not below / I was therefore / none other than / and not
is in no way below / I was therefore not / none other than / and not
falls far short of / I was therefore not / not / but rather
explanation: Professional-level playing by a child is amazing, as (2) says. (3) says the writer was not amazed; in (1) and (4) weak playing gives no reason for the reaction described.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The olive oil produced in the kibbutz ____ that of the neighboring kibbutz, and since it is ____ , it is ____ that most of the shops in the area prefer to buy the neighbors' oil.
choices: is much better than / cheaper / not surprising
is inferior to / more expensive / surprising
is in no way inferior to / more expensive / not surprising
is in no way inferior to / considerably cheaper / not surprising
explanation: Oil of equal quality at a higher price explains the shops' preference, as in (3). In (1) and (4) oil that is at least as good and cheaper should be preferred, so the preference is surprising; in (2) worse and more expensive oil explains the preference, so it is not surprising.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: In his review of the new collection by the poet Aharoni, the critic wrote: "Poems about nature ____ a formula for dull poetry, ____ the poet Levinson, ____ , Aharoni ____ ."
choices: are not necessarily / but unlike / whose nature poems are among the finest in the language / has not succeeded in giving them any life
are / and indeed, like / whose nature poems were forgotten long ago / has succeeded in making them fresh and original
are not necessarily / and indeed, like / who wrote such poems brilliantly / has written a dull collection
are / but unlike / whose nature poems are repetitive and dull / has failed to avoid this formula
explanation: Levinson shows that nature poems can succeed, and Aharoni, unlike him, fails, as in (1). In (3) "like" joins opposite results; in (4) "unlike" joins the same result; in (2) Aharoni's success contradicts "and indeed".
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Although the dialect spoken in the villages of the valley today is very different from the dialect spoken there a hundred years ago, ____ , since the change was ____ that ____ .
choices: the residents certainly felt that their language was changing / so slow / each generation spoke almost like its parents
the change was noticed only by visitors from outside / so fast / every generation spoke differently from its parents
the old residents complain that the young speak a different language / so gradual / the differences between parents and children were hardly noticeable
none of the generations felt that it spoke differently from its parents / so gradual / the differences between parents and children were small
explanation: A gradual change with small differences between parents and children explains why no generation felt a change, as in (4). In (1) a slow change does not explain the feeling of change; in (2) a fast change would be noticed by the residents themselves; in (3) complaints about a different language do not fit differences that were hardly noticeable.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Since the new road was opened, the vegetables of the valley reach the markets in the center of the country ____ , ____ their price there ____ .
choices: in half the time / and as a result / has dropped
in half the time / but / has dropped
only after long delays / and as a result / has dropped
in half the time / and as a result / has risen
explanation: Faster transport lowers the cost, and therefore the price, as in (1). In (2) "but" presents the drop as unexpected; in (3) delays do not explain a lower price; in (4) faster transport does not explain a higher price.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Lahav tells the students in his acting class to ____ , and in this he differs from most of his colleagues, who ____ . In his opinion, ____ .
choices: keep their own feelings out of the role / also ask students to keep their feelings out of the role / an actor who relies on his mood cannot repeat a good performance
draw on their own memories / demand the opposite / a performance built on the actor's mood changes from night to night
draw on their own memories / demand exactly the same / only an actor who truly feels can move the audience
keep their own feelings out of the role / demand the opposite / a performance built on the actor's mood changes from night to night
explanation: Lahav's instruction differs from his colleagues', and his reason supports it, as in (4). In (1) and (3) he demands the same as his colleagues although he is said to differ from them; in (2) his reason argues against his own instruction.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Professor Kedem ____ , and therefore it is not surprising that his letter, in which he wrote that Ella's research was ____ , ____ .
choices: writes letters of recommendation for almost anyone who asks / the best he had read in years / greatly impressed the committee
rarely agrees to write letters of recommendation / worth reading / greatly impressed the committee
praises almost no one / excellent / made no impression on the committee
writes warm letters for all his students / excellent / helped her more than any other letter
explanation: A letter from someone who rarely writes letters carries weight even in moderate words, as in (2). In (1) and (4) praise from someone who praises everyone gives no reason for its great effect; in (3) rare praise should have made an impression.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: If the plot of land in the north of the valley were ____ fertile than mine, but ____ the market, I ____ move my farm there, since distance from the market is ____ important to me than the quality of the soil.
choices: more / farther from / would not / more
less / closer to / would / less
more / farther from / would / more
less / closer to / would not / more
explanation: Better soil but a longer way to market is rejected, because distance matters more to the speaker than soil, as in (1). In (3) he moves although the drawback he cares about most is greater; in (2) he moves to worse soil although soil matters more to him; in (4) he refuses a plot that is closer to market, which he values most.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Some archaeologists complain that their colleagues ____ where the city wall stood ____ ; in their opinion, ____ .
choices: argue endlessly about / instead of reading the ancient texts more carefully / only digging will settle the question
have stopped arguing about / and have begun to dig / only digging will settle the question
argue endlessly about / on the basis of the ancient texts / only digging will settle the question
argue endlessly about / instead of digging / the texts contain everything that is needed
explanation: The complaint is about endless arguments over texts, and the remedy is digging, as in (3). In (1) the complaint asks for more reading, while the remedy is digging; in (2) the colleagues already dig, so there is nothing to complain about; in (4) the complaint asks for digging, while the opinion relies on the texts.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Unlike in the past, when letters from abroad ____ and people ____ , today ____ .
choices: took weeks to arrive / wrote long and detailed letters / when an answer can arrive within minutes, most messages are short
arrived within a few days / wrote short letters / people also write short messages
took weeks to arrive / wrote long and detailed letters / people write even longer letters than before, since the mail is still slow
took weeks to arrive / wrote only a few words / most messages are short
explanation: "Unlike in the past" requires a change, and slow mail explains the long letters of the past, as in (1). In (2), (3) and (4) nothing has changed: short letters then and short messages now, slow mail then and still slow mail now.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Even though Professor Elnatan usually ____ books on the history of the ancient world, the new book on ancient Egypt ____ ; ____ , he ____ .
choices: avoids reading / interested him greatly / and even so / recommended it to his students
enjoys reading / interested him greatly / and therefore / recommended it to his students
enjoys reading / did not interest him / and even so / did not advise his students against reading it
cannot stand / held his attention from beginning to end / and for this reason / advised his students not to read it
explanation: He likes such books but not this one, and still he does not discourage his students, as in (3). (2) has no contrast after "Even though"; in (1) "even so" joins interest and a recommendation; in (4) his advice contradicts his interest in the book.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem:
Na'or: "Fewer people come to the museum in winter because of the rain."
Chagit: "____ , since in winter the museum ____ , and still ____ ."
choices: You may be wrong / lowers its prices / fewer people come
You are probably right / lowers its prices / fewer people come
You are probably right / raises its prices / fewer people come
That cannot be the reason / offers free entry / people stay away
explanation: If fewer people come even though prices are lowered, the price cannot explain the drop, which supports Na'or, as in (2). In (1) and (4) the same kind of fact is said to count against him; in (3) higher prices offer another explanation, so they do not support him.
